question: In hard thresholding, what happens to a SNP whose P-value is above the threshold?

answers.answer: Its effect size is set to zero — it is left out of the score
answers.feedback: Right. Hard thresholding keeps SNPs below the threshold at their full GWAS effect and drops the rest.
Partial shrinkage is what soft thresholding does. Hard thresholding is all or nothing.

answers.answer: It is kept at its full GWAS effect size
answers.feedback: That happens to SNPs below the threshold.

question: What happens as the P-value threshold is raised from 5 × 10⁻⁸ to 0.05?

answers.answer: More variants are included, both more causal ones and many more null ones
answers.feedback: Right. In this module's simulation the count rose from 8 to 148 variants. The best threshold is chosen in validation data.
A higher (less strict) threshold lets more SNPs through.
A P-value cannot tell causal from null variants for certain; null SNPs also pass more lenient thresholds.

question: What distinguishes soft thresholding from hard thresholding?

answers.answer: It shrinks the effects of all variants toward zero instead of keeping or dropping each one
answers.feedback: Right. Examples are LASSO and Bayesian methods such as LDpred.

answers.answer: It uses a lower P-value threshold
answers.feedback: Soft thresholding does not rely on a single P-value cut-off at all.

answers.answer: It only uses genome-wide significant SNPs
answers.feedback: Soft thresholding typically includes far more variants — millions in genome-wide scores.

question: Under Bayesian shrinkage with a small assumed fraction of causal variants p, what happens to a large, highly significant effect estimate?

answers.answer: It is left almost unchanged, while small, noisy estimates are shrunk almost to zero
answers.feedback: Right. With small p the method expects a few real large effects and treats small estimates as noise.
Large, well-supported estimates are the ones the method keeps.

answers.answer: It is shrunk by the same proportion as every other estimate
answers.feedback: That is the behaviour with p = 1, the infinitesimal model.
